snapshot.stmt:
For every compatible encoded oracle family \(\mathbf M\), the enumerative algorithm satisfies \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M)\), is population sound and complete, and returns actual paired compatible certificates for every residual circle.  It terminates after checking at most \(3^{\binom D2}2^{2^D+DK}\) normalized certificates, with crude runtime
\[
O\!\left(3^{\binom D2}2^{2^D+DK}
\left[D2^D+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]\right).
\]
The observational output is on \(V\), each nonobservational certificate component is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), and no polynomial claim is made for this global search or for the conditional-independence and invariance queries needed to obtain \(\mathbf M\).  No completeness assertion is made for a fixed polynomial local CDIS calculus.

defs.def:complete-cdis:
Enumerate in a fixed lexicographic order all normalized Dai certificates \(\mathcal R=(E,H,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+})\) and retain precisely those satisfying \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1\).  If none passes, return the flag \(\mathsf{incompatible}\).  Otherwise, for every \(e=(k,u;uv)\in\mathcal E(\mathbf M)\), form the nonempty feasible-mark set
\[
B_e(\mathbf M)=\left\{\operatorname{mark}_e\bigl(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\bigr):\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1\right\}\subseteq\{\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{arrow}\}.
\]
Set the output mark at \(e\) to the unique element when \(B_e(\mathbf M)\) is a singleton and to a circle when it contains both marks.  For every circle, retain the first accepted tail certificate and the first accepted arrowhead certificate in the enumeration order.  Define \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)\) to be this partial-graph family together with those coupled certificates.  Its observational component is on \(V\); only a component indexed by \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).
defs.def:dai-certificate-checker:
For a normalized certificate \(\mathcal R=(E,H,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+})\), set
\[
A(\mathcal R)=\operatorname{an}_E\!\left(\bigcup_{h\in H}h\right),
\qquad
F_k(\mathcal R)=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k).
\]
Construct a fully oriented family \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R)=(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R),\ldots,\mathcal N^{(K)}(\mathcal R))\) as follows.  The observational graph \(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R)\) has vertex set \(V\).  Distinct \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when at least one of the following holds:
\[
i\to j\in E\text{ or }j\to i\in E;
\quad
\exists c\in A(\mathcal R):\ i\to c\leftarrow j\text{ in }E;
\quad
\exists h\in H:\ \{i,j\}\subseteq h.
\]
At an observational adjacency, the endpoint at \(i\) is a tail exactly when \(i\in A(\mathcal R)\) or \(i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)\), and is an arrowhead otherwise.

For \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the graph \(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\) has vertex set \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).  Vertices \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R)\), or there is a path \((i=v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_m=j)\) in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R)\) such that every \(v_\ell\) belongs to \(A(\mathcal R)\) and every internal vertex \(v_1,\ldots,v_{m-1}\) belongs to \(F_k(\mathcal R)\).  Also, \(\zeta_k\) is adjacent to \(j\) exactly when
\[
j\in T_k\cup\bigl(F_k(\mathcal R)\cap A(\mathcal R)\bigr),
\]
and every such edge is \(\zeta_k\to j\).  For an adjacency between \(i,j\in V\), preserve an observational directed orientation when one exists.  Otherwise orient it by the following exhaustive cases:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{condition}&\text{orientation}\\ \hline
i,j\notin F_k(\mathcal R)&i\mathbin{-}j\\
j\in F_k(\mathcal R),\ i\notin F_k(\mathcal R)\text{ or }i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)&i\to j\\
i\in F_k(\mathcal R),\ j\notin F_k(\mathcal R)\text{ or }j\in\operatorname{an}_E(i)&j\to i\\
i,j\in F_k(\mathcal R),\ i\notin\operatorname{an}_E(j),\ j\notin\operatorname{an}_E(i)&i\leftrightarrow j.
\end{array}
\]
Define \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1\) exactly when, for every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) have the same adjacency set and the same set of unshielded collider triples; otherwise set the checker to zero.  All ancestry, descendant, connectivity, adjacency, and unshielded-collider tests are finite matrix computations.  Regime zero introduces no indicator, whereas only \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) uses \(\zeta_k\).
defs.def:normalized-dai-certificate:
A normalized Dai certificate is a tuple
\[
\mathcal R=(E,H,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}),
\]
where \(E\) is a directed acyclic graph on \(V\), \(H\subseteq 2^V\) is a set of distinct subsets of \(V\), and \(T_k\subseteq V\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\); set \(T_0=\varnothing\).  A member \(h\in H\) represents the parent set of one binary childless selection node, and \(T_k\) represents the unknown soft-intervention target in regime \(k\).  In particular, \(|H|\le 2^D\).
defs.def:oracle-input-encoding: Encode \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) by one \(D\times D\) adjacency-mark matrix on \(V\), and encode each \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\), \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), by one \((D+1)\times(D+1)\) adjacency-mark matrix on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\). snapshot.stmt: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{ext}}\), can one construct a finite within- and cross-regime rule system \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\), independent of \(D,K\), such that every rule has the typed finite representation in \(\texttt{def:finite-rule-encoding}\), has per-scan cost \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\), and is sound over \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\); and such that for every endpoint \(e\) left circular by \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M))\) there exist \(\eta_e^{\mathrm t},\eta_e^{\mathrm a}\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) whose indicator-free observational projection and indicator-bearing nonobservational projections agree with every fixed closure mark while realizing respectively a tail and an arrowhead at \(e\)?

defs.def:extension-handle: Handle: start from the ordinary discriminating-path and uncovered-path closure inside each regime; attach the descendant and ancestral-selection labels forced by Dai et al.'s twin-MAG lemmas; propagate only label consequences shared across regimes; then adapt Jaber et al.'s I-MAG realizability lemma and Zhang's circle-component completion to construct, for a chosen unresolved endpoint, one tail completion and one arrowhead completion that are projections of a single common basal DAG with one ordered unknown-target family.
defs.def:finite-rule-encoding: Encode each \(r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) by a finite tuple of \(a_r\) typed regime placeholders, \(b_r\) typed vertex placeholders, adjacency and endpoint-mark premises, finite-state uncovered-path or discriminating-path predicates, and a nonempty list of circle-to-tail or circle-to-arrow updates. Regime placeholders are typed as either \(\{0\}\) or \(\mathcal K_+\), and an indicator term may occur only with the latter type. Match \(r\) by enumerating its regime and vertex assignments and deciding every path predicate by breadth-first search on its finite product-state graph. One exhaustive scan has cost \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\).
defs.def:initial-family: On the observational skeleton on \(V\), orient the supplied unshielded colliders. On each nonobservational skeleton indexed by \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), orient the supplied unshielded colliders and every endpoint at the existing indicator \(\zeta_k\) as a tail. No indicator endpoint is introduced in regime zero. Store the resulting family as adjacency and endpoint-mark matrices \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M)\); ordinary FCI closure and cross-regime propagation are both performed by \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\).
defs.def:mag-projection: Set \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)}=\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0);X_V,\varnothing,S_\eta^*)\), retaining exactly \(V\) and no intervention indicator. Separately, for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), set \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}=\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k);X_V\cup\{\zeta_k\},X^*\cup\varepsilon,S_\eta^*)\). In either branch, join two retained vertices exactly when an inducing path exists after the stated marginalization and conditioning, then place a tail at an endpoint exactly when that endpoint is an ancestor of the other endpoint or of \(S_\eta^*\), and an arrowhead otherwise.
defs.def:monotone-closure: \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathsf R}(\mathcal P)=\bigvee_{t\ge0}\mathsf R^t(\mathcal P)\), where the join is taken in the endpoint information order \(\circ\prec\mathrm{tail}\) and \(\circ\prec\mathrm{arrow}\), and every strict step fixes at least one previously circular endpoint.
defs.def:twin-graph: Define \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0)\) as the indicator-free selected observational DAG on reality vertices \(X_V\) and basal selection copies \(S_\eta^*\): copy \(\mathcal G_\eta[V]\) onto \(X_V\), copy each selection-parent edge into \(S_\eta^*\), and introduce no basal system copy, shared-noise vertex, or intervention-indicator vertex. Separately, for each \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), form \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k)\) on reality vertices \(X_V\), basal copies \(X_i^*\) and shared noises \(\varepsilon_i\) for \(i\in\operatorname{de}_{\mathcal G_\eta}(I_\eta^{(k)})\), basal selection copies \(S_\eta^*\), and \(\zeta_k\). Copy each edge of \(\mathcal G_\eta[V]\) into each available world, route unaffected parents into affected basal children, copy selection-parent edges only into \(S_\eta^*\), add \(\varepsilon_i\to X_i\) and \(\varepsilon_i\to X_i^*\), and add \(\zeta_k\to X_i\) exactly for \(i\in I_\eta^{(k)}\).

defs.def:dai-certificate-checker:
For a normalized certificate \(\mathcal R=(E,H,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+})\), set
\[
A(\mathcal R)=\operatorname{an}_E\!\left(\bigcup_{h\in H}h\right),
\qquad
F_k(\mathcal R)=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k).
\]
Construct a fully oriented family \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R)=(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R),\ldots,\mathcal N^{(K)}(\mathcal R))\) as follows.  The observational graph \(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R)\) has vertex set \(V\).  Distinct \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when at least one of the following holds:
\[
i\to j\in E\text{ or }j\to i\in E;
\quad
\exists c\in A(\mathcal R):\ i\to c\leftarrow j\text{ in }E;
\quad
\exists h\in H:\ \{i,j\}\subseteq h.
\]
At an observational adjacency, the endpoint at \(i\) is a tail exactly when \(i\in A(\mathcal R)\) or \(i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)\), and is an arrowhead otherwise.

For \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the graph \(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\) has vertex set \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).  Vertices \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R)\), or there is a path \((i=v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_m=j)\) in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R)\) such that every \(v_\ell\) belongs to \(A(\mathcal R)\) and every internal vertex \(v_1,\ldots,v_{m-1}\) belongs to \(F_k(\mathcal R)\).  Also, \(\zeta_k\) is adjacent to \(j\) exactly when
\[
j\in T_k\cup\bigl(F_k(\mathcal R)\cap A(\mathcal R)\bigr),
\]
and every such edge is \(\zeta_k\to j\).  For an adjacency between \(i,j\in V\), preserve an observational directed orientation when one exists.  Otherwise orient it by the following exhaustive cases:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{condition}&\text{orientation}\\ \hline
i,j\notin F_k(\mathcal R)&i\mathbin{-}j\\
j\in F_k(\mathcal R),\ i\notin F_k(\mathcal R)\text{ or }i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)&i\to j\\
i\in F_k(\mathcal R),\ j\notin F_k(\mathcal R)\text{ or }j\in\operatorname{an}_E(i)&j\to i\\
i,j\in F_k(\mathcal R),\ i\notin\operatorname{an}_E(j),\ j\notin\operatorname{an}_E(i)&i\leftrightarrow j.
\end{array}
\]
Define \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1\) exactly when, for every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) have the same adjacency set and the same set of unshielded collider triples; otherwise set the checker to zero.  All ancestry, descendant, connectivity, adjacency, and unshielded-collider tests are finite matrix computations.  Regime zero introduces no indicator, whereas only \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) uses \(\zeta_k\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every compatible encoded oracle family \(\mathbf M\), the enumerative algorithm satisfies \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M)\), is population sound and complete, and returns actual paired compatible certificates for every residual circle.  It terminates after checking at most \(6^{\binom D2}2^{D+DK}\) normalized Dai two-section certificates, with crude runtime
\[
O\!\left(6^{\binom D2}2^{D+DK}
\left[D^2+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]\right).
\]
The global search is singly exponential in \(D^2+DK\).  The observational output is on \(V\), each nonobservational certificate component is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), and no polynomial claim is made for this global search or for the conditional-independence and invariance queries needed to obtain \(\mathbf M\). defs.def:complete-cdis:
Enumerate in a fixed lexicographic order all normalized Dai two-section certificates \(\mathcal R=(E,A,Q,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+})\) and retain precisely those satisfying \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1\).  If none passes, return the flag \(\mathsf{incompatible}\).  Otherwise, for every \(e=(k,u;uv)\in\mathcal E(\mathbf M)\), form the nonempty feasible-mark set
\[
B_e(\mathbf M)=\left\{\operatorname{mark}_e\bigl(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\bigr):\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1\right\}\subseteq\{\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{arrow}\}.
\]
Set the output mark at \(e\) to the unique element when \(B_e(\mathbf M)\) is a singleton and to a circle when it contains both marks.  For every circle, retain the first accepted tail certificate and the first accepted arrowhead certificate in the enumeration order.  Define \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)\) to be this partial-graph family together with those coupled certificates.  Its observational component is on \(V\); only a component indexed by \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).
defs.def:dai-certificate-checker:
For a normalized certificate \(\mathcal R=(E,A,Q,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+})\), set
\[
F_k(\mathcal R)=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k).
\]
Construct a fully oriented family \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R)=(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R),\ldots,\mathcal N^{(K)}(\mathcal R))\) as follows.  The observational graph \(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R)\) has vertex set \(V\).  Distinct \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when at least one of the following holds:
\[
i\to j\in E\text{ or }j\to i\in E;
\quad
\exists c\in A:\ i\to c\leftarrow j\text{ in }E;
\quad
\{i,j\}\in Q.
\]
At an observational adjacency, the endpoint at \(i\) is a tail exactly when \(i\in A\) or \(i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)\), and is an arrowhead otherwise.

For \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the graph \(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\) has vertex set \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).  Vertices \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R)\), or there is a path \((i=v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_m=j)\) in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R)\) such that every \(v_\ell\) belongs to \(A\) and every internal vertex \(v_1,\ldots,v_{m-1}\) belongs to \(F_k(\mathcal R)\).  Also, \(\zeta_k\) is adjacent to \(j\) exactly when
\[
j\in T_k\cup\bigl(F_k(\mathcal R)\cap A\bigr),
\]
and every such edge is \(\zeta_k\to j\).  For an adjacency between \(i,j\in V\), preserve an observational directed orientation when one exists.  Otherwise orient it by the following exhaustive cases:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{condition}&\text{orientation}\\ \hline
i,j\notin F_k(\mathcal R)&i\mathbin{-}j\\
j\in F_k(\mathcal R),\ i\notin F_k(\mathcal R)\text{ or }i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)&i\to j\\
i\in F_k(\mathcal R),\ j\notin F_k(\mathcal R)\text{ or }j\in\operatorname{an}_E(i)&j\to i\\
i,j\in F_k(\mathcal R),\ i\notin\operatorname{an}_E(j),\ j\notin\operatorname{an}_E(i)&i\leftrightarrow j.
\end{array}
\]
Define \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1\) exactly when, for every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) have the same adjacency set and the same set of unshielded collider triples; otherwise set the checker to zero.  All ancestor-closure, descendant, connectivity, adjacency, endpoint, and unshielded-collider tests are finite matrix computations.  Regime zero introduces no indicator, whereas only \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) uses \(\zeta_k\).
defs.def:normalized-dai-certificate:
A normalized Dai two-section certificate is a tuple
\[
\mathcal R=(E,A,Q,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}),
\]
where \(E\) is a directed acyclic graph on \(V\), \(A\subseteq V\) is ancestor-closed in \(E\), meaning \(\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A\), \(Q\subseteq\binom{A}{2}\) is a simple undirected graph, and \(T_k\subseteq V\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\); set \(T_0=\varnothing\).  The set \(A\) represents the observed ancestors of the conditioned selection nodes, \(Q\) records the unordered pairs that share at least one conditioned selection child, and \(T_k\) is the unknown soft-intervention target in regime \(k\).

defs.def:dai-certificate-checker:

\[
Q=Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=S_0(\mathbf M)\setminus B(E,A),
\qquad
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}=\bigl(E,A,Q,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\bigr),
\qquad
F_k(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M})=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k).
\]
Construct \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M})=(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}),\ldots,\mathcal N^{(K)}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}))\) as follows.  The observational graph has vertex set \(V\); distinct \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when
\[

\quad\text{or}\quad
\exists c\in A:\ i\to c\leftarrow j\text{ in }E,
\quad\text{or}\quad

\]

\[
j\in T_k\cup\bigl(F_k(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M})\cap A\bigr),
\]
and every such edge is \(\zeta_k\to j\).  For an adjacency between \(i,j\in V\), preserve an observational directed orientation when one exists.  Otherwise orient it by the following exhaustive cases:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{condition}&\text{orientation}\\ \hline
i,j\notin F_k(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M})&i\mathbin{-}j\\
j\in F_k(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}),\ i\notin F_k(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M})\text{ or }i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)&i\to j\\

defs.def:normalized-dai-certificate:
Given the encoded oracle family \(\mathbf M\), write \(S_0(\mathbf M)=E(\mathcal M^{(0)})\) for its observational adjacency set.  For a directed acyclic graph \(E\) on \(V\) and a set \(A\subseteq V\), define
\[
B(E,A)=\left\{\{i,j\}\in\binom V2:
i\to j\in E\ \text{or}\ j\to i\in E\ \text{or}\
\exists c\in A:\ i\to c\leftarrow j\ \text{in }E
\right\}.
\]
An input-conditioned normalized Dai two-section certificate is
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}=\bigl(E,A,Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\bigr),
\qquad
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=S_0(\mathbf M)\setminus B(E,A),
\]
where \(\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A\), \(B(E,A)\subseteq S_0(\mathbf M)\), \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\subseteq\binom A2\), and \(T_k\subseteq V\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\); set \(T_0=\varnothing\).  Thus \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) is uniquely derived from \((\mathbf M,E,A)\) and is not an independently enumerated coordinate.  It records exactly those supplied observational adjacencies not already generated by a basal edge or by an observed collider child in \(A\).

Neither \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) nor any target set is independently enumerated.  When \(K=0\), the tuple has no nonobservational coordinate and no objects \(Z_k,R_k,O_k,T^*_{k,\mathbf M},F^*_{k,\mathbf M}\) are introduced; set only the observational target to \(T_0^*=\varnothing\).
defs.def:dai-certificate-checker:
Given \(\mathbf M\), enumerate a pair \((E,A)\) and reject it unless it is residual-admissible under \(\texttt{def:normalized-dai-certificate}\).  For a survivor derive, rather than enumerate,
\[
Q=Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\qquad
T_k^*=T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A),
\qquad
F_k^*=F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k^*)
\quad(k\in\mathcal K_+),
\]
and set
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=
\left(E,A,Q,(T_k^*)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right).
\]
Construct \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M})=(\mathcal N^{(0)},\ldots,\mathcal N^{(K)})\) as follows.  The observational graph has vertex set \(V\); distinct \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when
\[
i\to j\in E\text{ or }j\to i\in E,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\exists c\in A:\ i\to c\leftarrow j\text{ in }E,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\{i,j\}\in Q.
\]
Its adjacency set is \(B(E,A)\cup Q=S_0(\mathbf M)\).  At an observational adjacency, the endpoint at \(i\) is a tail exactly when \(i\in A\) or \(i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)\), and is an arrowhead otherwise.

For \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the graph \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) has vertex set \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).  Vertices \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\), or there is a path \((i=v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_m=j)\) in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\) such that every \(v_\ell\) belongs to \(A\) and every internal vertex belongs to \(F_k^*\).  The indicator \(\zeta_k\) is adjacent to \(j\) exactly when
\[
j\in T_k^*\cup(F_k^*\cap A)=Z_k(\mathbf M),
\]
and every such edge is \(\zeta_k\to j\).  For an adjacency between \(i,j\in V\), preserve an observational directed orientation when one exists.  Otherwise orient it by the exhaustive cases
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{condition}&\text{orientation}\\ \hline
i,j\notin F_k^*&i\mathbin{-}j\\
j\in F_k^*,\ i\notin F_k^*\text{ or }i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)&i\to j\\
i\in F_k^*,\ j\notin F_k^*\text{ or }j\in\operatorname{an}_E(i)&j\to i\\
i,j\in F_k^*,\ i\notin\operatorname{an}_E(j),\ j\notin\operatorname{an}_E(i)&i\leftrightarrow j.
\end{array}
\]
Define \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1\) exactly when, for every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) have the same adjacency set and the same unshielded collider triples; otherwise set it to zero.  All tests and all derived sets are finite matrix computations.  If \(K=0\), construct and compare only the indicator-free observational graph and introduce no \(Z_k,R_k,O_k,T_k^*\), or \(F_k^*\).
defs.def:oracle-input-encoding: Encode \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) by one \(D\times D\) adjacency-mark matrix on \(V\), and encode each \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\), \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), by one \((D+1)\times(D+1)\) adjacency-mark matrix on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\). The representation length is \(L_{\mathrm{in}}=D^2+K(D+1)^2\), and regime zero has no row or column for an indicator.

assumptions.ass:compatible-input: The supplied family has at least one compatible model: \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing\).

snapshot.stmt: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{ext}}\), can one construct a finite within- and cross-regime rule system \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\), independent of \(D,K\), such that every rule has the typed finite representation in \(\texttt{def:finite-rule-encoding}\), has per-scan cost \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\), and is sound over \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\); and such that for every endpoint \(e\) left circular by \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M))\) there exist \(\eta_e^{\mathrm t},\eta_e^{\mathrm a}\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) whose indicator-free observational projection and indicator-bearing nonobservational projections agree with every fixed closure mark while realizing respectively a tail and an arrowhead at \(e\)?

defs.def:extension-handle: Handle: start from the ordinary discriminating-path and uncovered-path closure inside each regime; attach the descendant and ancestral-selection labels forced by Dai et al.'s twin-MAG lemmas; propagate only label consequences shared across regimes; then adapt Jaber et al.'s I-MAG realizability lemma and Zhang's circle-component completion to construct, for a chosen unresolved endpoint, one tail completion and one arrowhead completion that are projections of a single common basal DAG with one ordered unknown-target family.
defs.def:finite-rule-encoding: Encode each \(r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) by a finite tuple of \(a_r\) typed regime placeholders, \(b_r\) typed vertex placeholders, adjacency and endpoint-mark premises, finite-state uncovered-path or discriminating-path predicates, and a nonempty list of circle-to-tail or circle-to-arrow updates. Regime placeholders are typed as either \(\{0\}\) or \(\mathcal K_+\), and an indicator term may occur only with the latter type. Match \(r\) by enumerating its regime and vertex assignments and deciding every path predicate by breadth-first search on its finite product-state graph. One exhaustive scan has cost \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\).
defs.def:initial-family: On the observational skeleton on \(V\), orient the supplied unshielded colliders. On each nonobservational skeleton indexed by \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), orient the supplied unshielded colliders and every endpoint at the existing indicator \(\zeta_k\) as a tail. No indicator endpoint is introduced in regime zero. Store the resulting family as adjacency and endpoint-mark matrices \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M)\); ordinary FCI closure and cross-regime propagation are both performed by \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\).
defs.def:mag-projection: Set \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)}=\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0);X_V,\varnothing,S_\eta^*)\), retaining exactly \(V\) and no intervention indicator. Separately, for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), set \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}=\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k);X_V\cup\{\zeta_k\},X^*\cup\varepsilon,S_\eta^*)\). In either branch, join two retained vertices exactly when an inducing path exists after the stated marginalization and conditioning, then place a tail at an endpoint exactly when that endpoint is an ancestor of the other endpoint or of \(S_\eta^*\), and an arrowhead otherwise.
defs.def:monotone-closure: \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathsf R}(\mathcal P)=\bigvee_{t\ge0}\mathsf R^t(\mathcal P)\), where the join is taken in the endpoint information order \(\circ\prec\mathrm{tail}\) and \(\circ\prec\mathrm{arrow}\), and every strict step fixes at least one previously circular endpoint.
defs.def:twin-graph: Define \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0)\) as the indicator-free selected observational DAG on reality vertices \(X_V\) and basal selection copies \(S_\eta^*\): copy \(\mathcal G_\eta[V]\) onto \(X_V\), copy each selection-parent edge into \(S_\eta^*\), and introduce no basal system copy, shared-noise vertex, or intervention-indicator vertex. Separately, for each \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), form \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k)\) on reality vertices \(X_V\), basal copies \(X_i^*\) and shared noises \(\varepsilon_i\) for \(i\in\operatorname{de}_{\mathcal G_\eta}(I_\eta^{(k)})\), basal selection copies \(S_\eta^*\), and \(\zeta_k\). Copy each edge of \(\mathcal G_\eta[V]\) into each available world, route unaffected parents into affected basal children, copy selection-parent edges only into \(S_\eta^*\), add \(\varepsilon_i\to X_i\) and \(\varepsilon_i\to X_i^*\), and add \(\zeta_k\to X_i\) exactly for \(i\in I_\eta^{(k)}\).

assumptions.ass:compatible-input: The supplied family has at least one compatible model: \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing\).
assumptions.ass:finite-dag: For candidate \(\eta\), \(\mathcal G_\eta\) is a finite directed acyclic graph on \(V\cup S_\eta\).
assumptions.ass:causal-sufficiency: Candidate \(\eta\) contains no latent common cause of two vertices in \(V\).
assumptions.ass:selection-childless: Every vertex in \(S_\eta\) has no child in \(\mathcal G_\eta\).
assumptions.ass:selection-parents: Every parent in \(\mathcal G_\eta\) of a vertex in \(S_\eta\) belongs to \(V\).
assumptions.ass:selected-stratum: The observed stratum for candidate \(\eta\) conditions on \(S_\eta=\mathbf 1\).
assumptions.ass:pretreatment-selection: The conditioned selection-node set in \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0)\) and in \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k)\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) equals the basal copy \(S_\eta^*\).
assumptions.ass:observational-target: The observational regime has empty intervention target \(I_\eta^{(0)}=\varnothing\).
assumptions.ass:soft-intervention-modularity: For each \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), every structural mechanism outside \(I_\eta^{(k)}\) and its exogenous input are shared with the basal world.
assumptions.ass:observational-equivalence-match: The indicator-free observational projection \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)}\) on \(V\) is Markov equivalent to the supplied observational representative \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\).
assumptions.ass:interventional-equivalence-match: For every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the projected twin MAG \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}\) on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) is Markov equivalent to the supplied nonobservational representative \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\).
